high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Reveals Reason for Withdrawing Funds from State-Owned Banks; Bank Indonesia Signals Not to Interfere in Monetary Policy
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa disclosed that his decision to withdraw Surplus Budget Balance (SAL) funds from state-owned banks (Himbara) was driven by a signal from Bank Indonesia to avoid interfering with monetary policy. BI reportedly asked the government to reduce its funds in state banks, promising to replace the liquidity through its own mechanisms. This revelation highlights the tension between fiscal and monetary policy coordination, which is significant for banking sector liquidity and investor confidence in Indonesia's macroeconomic management.

high.title: 9 Conglomerate Stocks Dominated by Handful of Shareholders – Full List
high.summary: Indonesian stocks are being removed from MSCI and FTSE Russell global indices due to high shareholding concentration (HSC), a category applied to shares where ownership is heavily concentrated among a few parties. BEI Director Jeffrey Hendrik acknowledged the issue and emphasized the exchange's preference for stocks to be included in global indices through proper and legitimate means. This development has significant implications for foreign capital flows into Indonesian equities and market credibility.

high.title: 9 Conglomerate Stocks Flagged for High Shareholding Concentration – Complete List
high.summary: Multiple conglomerate-owned stocks, including BREN (97.31% concentration), DSSA (95.76%), and DCII (99.96%), have been classified under the High Shareholding Concentration (HSC) category following BEI's inclusion of price impact ratio in its methodology. These stocks face potential exclusion from major global indices such as MSCI and FTSE Russell, which could trigger significant foreign investor sell-offs. This raises broader concerns about corporate governance and market depth in Indonesia's capital markets.

high.title: Trump Blockades Iranian Ports, Threatens to Strike Power Plants and Bridges
high.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has reinstated a full blockade of Iranian ports and threatened to attack power plants and bridges if Iran refuses to return to nuclear negotiations. The escalation of U.S.-Iran tensions poses significant risks to global energy supply chains and oil prices, which directly impact Indonesia's energy import costs and inflation outlook. Investors should monitor crude oil price movements as this geopolitical development could drive market volatility globally.

high.title: US Dollar Still Holding at Rp 18,000 Level
high.summary: The US dollar weakened slightly against the Indonesian Rupiah, trading at Rp 18,065, down 26 points (0.14%) as of Wednesday morning. The dollar also showed broad weakness against other major currencies including the Japanese Yen, Australian Dollar, British Pound, Euro, Singapore Dollar, and Chinese Yuan. The Rp 18,000 level remains a key psychological threshold for Indonesian businesses and importers managing currency risk.

high.title: Indonesia's Foreign Debt Nearly Reaches Rp 8,000 Trillion — Finance Minister Responds
high.summary: Indonesia's external debt has climbed to US$ 444.4 billion (approximately Rp 7,999 trillion at Rp 18,000/USD), reflecting 2.1% year-on-year growth according to Bank Indonesia data. Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa urged stakeholders to assess debt relative to the country's economic capacity rather than in absolute terms, arguing the debt-to-GDP ratio is the more meaningful metric. This near-breach of the Rp 8,000 trillion mark is a significant indicator for sovereign risk assessment and investor confidence in Indonesian fiscal management.

high.title: Free Nutritious Meals Program (MBG) to Be Discontinued for Children from Wealthy Families
high.summary: The National Nutrition Agency (BGN) announced it will stop providing the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program to school children from upper-income households, specifically those in social deciles 8 through 10. The policy reform was discussed directly by President Prabowo Subianto in a closed cabinet meeting on Wednesday, signaling a significant retargeting of one of the government's flagship social spending programs. This restructuring could affect the program's budget allocation and its downstream impact on food suppliers and catering businesses contracted under MBG.

high.title: Danantara Eyes Stake in Indonesia Stock Exchange Amid Demutualization Plans
high.summary: Indonesia's sovereign investment body Danantara has expressed interest in becoming a shareholder of the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) as OJK targets completing demutualization regulations by September 2026. Danantara CEO Rosan Roeslani stated the move aims to improve exchange governance, transparency, and accountability. This is a significant structural development for Indonesian capital markets as it opens IDX ownership to the public.

high.title: Finance Minister Defends Moving Surplus Budget Funds to State Banks Without DPR Approval
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa defended his decision to transfer State Budget Surplus (SAL) funds from Bank Indonesia to state-owned banks (Himbara) without parliamentary approval, asserting no regulatory changes require such consent. The move drew criticism from the DPR Commission XI, creating political tension over fiscal management authority. This has implications for liquidity in state banks and the broader government cash management strategy.

high.title: Indonesia Joins Global AI Cooperation Organization WAICO During Airlangga's China Visit
high.summary: Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto signed the founding agreement of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO) in Shanghai, marking Indonesia as one of the founding members. WAICO is designed to set global AI governance standards and ethical frameworks, and Indonesia's participation signals a strategic commitment to positioning itself as a key player in the global digital economy. This could attract digital investment and accelerate Indonesia's AI and tech sector development.

high.title: Indonesia's Foreign Debt Approaches Rp 8,000 Trillion — Finance Minister Responds
high.summary: Indonesia's external debt has risen 2.1% year-on-year to US$444.4 billion (approximately Rp 7,999 trillion at Rp 18,000/USD), nearing the Rp 8,000 trillion threshold. Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa urged stakeholders to assess debt relative to economic capacity rather than in absolute terms, drawing an analogy to corporate credit lines scaled by revenue. This debt level and the minister's response are critical signals for sovereign risk assessment and investor sentiment toward Indonesian government bonds.

high.title: Antam Gold Price Reverses Course, Falls After Yesterday's Rp 20,000 Surge
high.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices dropped Rp 2,000 per gram to Rp 2,633,000 today, reversing part of yesterday's sharp Rp 20,000 gain. Over the past week, prices have ranged between Rp 2,615,000 and Rp 2,655,000, while the buyback price also fell Rp 2,000 to Rp 2,380,000 per gram. Gold price volatility is a key indicator for Indonesian retail investors and serves as a gauge of broader safe-haven demand.

high.title: JCI Closes Higher, Rises to Level 6,108
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (JCI/IHSG) closed in positive territory on Thursday, July 16, 2026, rising 66 points (1.10%) to close at 6,108. The index reached its highest level at 6,108 during the session, with total transaction value reaching Rp 13.31 trillion involving 30.29 billion shares traded. This marks a meaningful recovery and is closely watched by investors as a key indicator of broader market sentiment.

high.title: BTN Records Net Profit of Rp 2.40 Trillion, Up 40.8% Year-on-Year in H1 2026
high.summary: State-owned mortgage bank PT Bank Tabungan Negara (BTN) posted a consolidated net profit of Rp 2.40 trillion in the first half of 2026, a strong 40.8% year-on-year growth. Total credit and financing disbursements reached Rp 418.11 trillion (up 11.2% YoY), driven by a 4.8% rise in housing loans and a significant 46.1% surge in non-housing loans. The results signal robust performance aligned with Danantara's transformation agenda and the government's 3 million homes program, making it a key positive development for BBTN shareholders.

high.title: Danantara Eyes Stake in Indonesia Stock Exchange Amid Demutualization Push
high.summary: Indonesia's sovereign investment body, Danantara (BPI), has expressed interest in becoming a shareholder of the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX/BEI) as part of the government's demutualization initiative, with OJK targeting related regulations to be finalized by September. Danantara CEO Rosan Roeslani stated the move aims to improve governance, transparency, and accountability of Indonesia's capital market infrastructure. This is a significant structural development for Indonesia's capital markets that could reshape ownership and oversight of the exchange.

medium.title: State-Owned Shipyard PT Dok dan Perkapalan Surabaya Declared Bankrupt; Danantara Plans Asset Takeover and Consolidation with PT PAL
medium.summary: State-owned shipyard PT Dok dan Perkapalan Surabaya (DPS) was declared bankrupt in early July 2026. Danantara's COO Dony Oskaria confirmed that the company's assets will be taken over and consolidated under PT PAL, Indonesia's primary state-owned shipbuilder. This restructuring signals Danantara's broader strategy to consolidate all state-owned shipyard assets under a single entity, which could impact the maritime and defense industry sector.

medium.title: Reports Circulate of Peruri Director Replacement by Retired Military Officer; Danantara COO Responds
medium.summary: Reports have emerged that Dwina Septiani Wijaya, the current Director of Perum Peruri (Indonesia's state-owned currency and security printing company), is being replaced by a retired military officer. Danantara's COO acknowledged that a leadership change at Peruri had been planned, though he had not yet confirmed the details. Changes in leadership at a strategically sensitive state enterprise like Peruri may raise governance and operational continuity concerns for investors.

medium.title: House of Representatives Commission XI Chair Rejects Claims That Danantara Bonds (Patriot Bond & Merah Putih Bond) Are a Money Laundering Vehicle
medium.summary: Commission XI Chair Misbakhun pushed back against narratives that Danantara's bond issuances — the Patriot Bond and Merah Putih Bond — could be used for money laundering, noting that bond purchases go through regulated intermediaries such as asset managers, securities firms, and bond brokers, each with their own KYC processes. The controversy arose because the government stated it would not verify the source of funds for bond purchases. This debate is relevant for investors considering exposure to Danantara-issued debt instruments and for assessing Indonesia's financial compliance framework.

medium.title: Danantara Interested in Owning Stake in Indonesia Stock Exchange – What Percentage?
medium.summary: Danantara CEO Rosan Roeslani confirmed the sovereign wealth fund's interest in becoming a shareholder of the Indonesia Stock Exchange (BEI) as part of the government's demutualization initiative. OJK is targeting completion of demutualization regulations by September, which would open BEI ownership to the public and institutional investors. Danantara's involvement is seen as a move to improve governance, transparency, and accountability of the Indonesian capital market.

medium.title: Prabowo Sets Rp 500 Million Fee for Notaries Transferring Work Area to Jakarta
medium.summary: President Prabowo has enacted Government Regulation No. 30/2026 establishing non-tax state revenue (PNBP) fees for notaries seeking to transfer their jurisdiction, with fees reaching up to Rp 500 million for transfers to Jakarta, effective August 1, 2026. Transfers to Category B regions are set at Rp 50 million and Category C regions at Rp 25 million per person. This regulatory change affects the legal and notarial services sector and increases the cost of business relocation for legal professionals in Indonesia.

medium.title: Antam Gold Price Reverses Lower After Yesterday's Rp 20,000 Jump
medium.summary: Antam's 24-karat gold price fell Rp 2,000 per gram to Rp 2,633,000 on Thursday, reversing part of the previous day's sharp Rp 20,000 gain. Over the past week, prices have ranged between Rp 2,615,000 and Rp 2,655,000 per gram, while the buyback price also dipped Rp 2,000 to Rp 2,380,000 per gram. The continued elevated gold price environment remains relevant for retail investors and those tracking safe-haven asset trends in Indonesia.

medium.title: Retired TNI General Teguh Arief Appointed as New Director of Peruri (State Printing Company)
medium.summary: Lieutenant General (Ret.) Teguh Arief Indratmoko has been appointed as the new President Director of Perum Peruri, replacing Dwina Septiani Wijaya, effective July 15, 2026, based on decrees issued by the State-Owned Enterprise Supervisory Board (BP BUMN). The leadership change at Peruri, Indonesia's state-owned security printing company responsible for printing currency and official documents, signals continued military-to-civilian enterprise appointments under the current administration. Investors tracking BUMN (state-owned enterprise) governance and leadership trends should note this development.

medium.title: Each Merah Putih Cooperative to Receive Rp 3 Billion Capital — Finance Minister Says It's Sufficient
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya confirmed that each Merah Putih Cooperative unit will receive Rp 3 billion in capital, sourced from loans through state-owned banks (Himbara), which he says is sufficient for both infrastructure construction and operational costs. The program represents a significant government initiative channeling state bank credit into grassroots cooperative development across Indonesia. Investors should monitor the credit exposure of Himbara banks and the fiscal implications of this large-scale cooperative funding program.

medium.title: Agrinas Boss Assures Village Cooperatives Will Boost, Not Hurt, Local Warung Businesses
medium.summary: PT Agrinas Pangan Nusantara's director assured that the Merah Putih Village Cooperative (KDKMP) program is designed to shorten distribution chains and lower goods prices for rural areas, benefiting rather than competing with local small shops (warung). The cooperatives aim to give rural retailers access to goods at fairer prices by eliminating lengthy distribution middlemen. This development is relevant for FMCG and distribution sector players as it signals a government-driven restructuring of rural supply chains.

medium.title: Retired TNI Lieutenant General Teguh Arief Appointed as New Director of Peruri (State Printing Company)
medium.summary: Lieutenant General (Ret.) Teguh Arief Indratmoko has been appointed as the new President Director of Perum Peruri, replacing Dwina Septiani Wijaya, effective July 15, 2026, per a decree from the State-Owned Enterprise Supervisory Board (BP BUMN). The appointment of a retired military officer to lead the state security printing company signals a strategic shift in leadership direction for the BUMN. This change may affect Peruri's operational and business strategy, relevant to stakeholders in the state enterprise ecosystem.

medium.title: Free Nutritious Meals Program (MBG) to Exclude Children from Wealthy Families
medium.summary: The National Nutrition Agency (BGN) announced it will stop distributing the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program to children from upper-income households, specifically those in socioeconomic deciles 8–10, following a cabinet-level discussion led by President Prabowo. This targeting reform aims to improve the efficiency and fiscal sustainability of one of the government's flagship social spending programs. The policy adjustment has implications for the program's budget allocation and its broader impact on food industry suppliers participating in MBG.

medium.title: International Money Transfers Made Easier with BRImo — Cashback Up to Rp 50,000
medium.summary: Bank BRI's mobile banking app, BRImo, has expanded its international transfer feature to cover more than 160 countries, positioning itself as a competitive digital remittance solution. The service includes a cashback promotion of up to Rp 50,000 to attract users sending money abroad for education, family support, or cross-border business. This development reflects BRI's push to grow its digital financial services revenue and compete in the remittance market.

medium.title: Indika Energy (INDY) Responds to Reports of Rp 17.9 Trillion Subsidiary Divestiture
medium.summary: PT Indika Energy Tbk (INDY) has declined to comment on market speculation regarding the potential divestiture of its coal subsidiary PT Kideco Jaya Agung at a reported value of US$1 billion (approximately Rp 17.97 trillion). The company's head of corporate communications stated the firm does not respond to market rumors or speculation. Investors in INDY should monitor this closely, as a confirmed transaction of this scale would be a major corporate event significantly impacting the company's asset portfolio and valuation.

medium.title: Mitratel (MTEL) Distributes 98% of Net Profit as Dividend, Totaling Rp 2.08 Trillion
medium.summary: PT Dayamitra Telekomunikasi Tbk (MTEL/Mitratel) approved a cash dividend of Rp 2.08 trillion (Rp 25.6 per share), representing 98% of its 2025 net profit, as decided at its Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (AGMS). The company reported full-year 2025 revenue of Rp 9.53 trillion, EBITDA of Rp 7.83 trillion, and net profit of Rp 2.12 trillion, supported by a strong recurring revenue model and an expanded fiber optic network totaling 57,199 km. The near-full payout ratio makes MTEL highly attractive for dividend-seeking investors.
